payload.claim: _in_cell_concerns rebuilds a REVIEW-time finding using only the file/line/claim stored in the findings table, then qualify() re-anchors it against the layer's final packaged diff (fields.head^..fields.head, lines 259-266). If the same task's REBUT phase fixed a blocker with an edit in the same file (rebut.run_rebut lets the implementer commit further changes, session.py:2714-2793), lines below that edit shift between the moment the concern was filed and the final head. _is_anchored (agents/findings.py:149-166) keys anchoring purely on the finding's stored line number, so a shifted concern can be silently dropped as unanchored, or coincidentally re-anchored to unrelated content that happens to share a token, producing a bogus qualification. Nothing in this diff recomputes or revalidates an in-cell concern's line against the code REBUT actually left behind, and no fixture here simulates a REBUT-driven line shift in the same file as a live concern, so the gates cannot see it.
